regime: Risk-Off Selloff, Oil Shock Leads (Crude +7.5%, Equities Heavy, Gold Flips Down)
summary: An oil shock ran the tape today. Crude ripped 7.5 percent to 103.94 on Middle East supply fears, and that dragged everything else. NQ lost 29,358 and closed 29,142, down 1.08 percent, and ES eased to 7,602, both below falling stops. Gold fell 2 percent to 4,358 and flipped its trend back down. August PPI ran 5.4 percent, a touch hot with softer core, VIX jumped to about 17.8, and CPI lands Friday.
psychology: Shock days set two traps, and most traders step in one. The first is chasing crude after a 7.5 percent run because it has to keep going. The second is fading the equity selloff because it went too far. Both fight a tape that just repriced in one morning. When one headline moves everything at once, your normal edge is not there, the range is twice as wide, and the next print is tomorrow. Smaller size or the sidelines is the position that survives to trade the reaction you can see. Let CPI print, then trade what the market does with it.

event.name: August PPI (released today) plus a Middle East crude supply shock
event.consensus: August PPI expected near 0.3 percent on the month. The bigger unscheduled driver was oil, on escalating Middle East tension.
event.actual: PPI ran 0.4 percent on the month and 5.4 percent on the year, a touch above expectations, with softer core at 0.2 percent and most of the rise from energy. Crude spiked about 7.5 percent on reports of attacks on Saudi energy facilities and a broader conflict.
event.surprise: Headline PPI a touch hot, core softer, so a mixed inflation read. The clean surprise was the oil supply shock, which is both an inflation and a growth worry.
event.nqReaction: NQ broke up out of the opening range, failed, and sold off to close 29,142, down 1.08 percent and below its falling stop. Rate sensitive tech fell more than ES.
event.crossAsset: Crude up 7.5 percent to 103.94 and leading. December gold down 2 percent to 4,358 and flipped its trend down, an odd risk-off tell that points to a yield and liquidation move. VIX up about 8 percent to roughly 17.8. August CPI lands Friday, the Fed decides September 16.

risk.sizing: Keep index size minimal. This was a fast, event driven, high volatility day with a geopolitical oil shock, and CPI prints in the morning. The indices are below falling stops, so the short term index trend is down. Both chasing an extended crude spike and fading a one way selloff carry outsized risk here. Crude is the one clean long above a rising 101.23 stop, but a 7.5 percent day is not a spot to add size into.
risk.openRisk: For the indices the falling stops are the line. MNQ back above 29,264 or MES above 7,620 on two hourly closes is the first sign the selling paused. Below, MNQ 29,097 then the 29,000 psych, and MES 7,585 then 7,550, are the downside. December gold is back below its 4,410 stop, with 4,355 then 4,300 the downside and 4,410 the first repair. Crude stays long above 101.23 and 100, and a close below 100 says the spike is unwinding.
risk.note: Rising event risk into August CPI Friday September 11 at 8:30 ET, with the Fed the following week. Keep size sensible and mind prop news blackout rules around the release. Not financial advice.

setups.bias: The up break failed and handed off to a downside trend below NYVWAP, this edge's shape. Manage tight into CPI.

setups.entry: Fade a failed break back inside the opening range
setups.t1: The opposite side of the range
setups.bias: NQ broke up out of the range, failed, and closed back inside near the low, though price kept leaking lower rather than settling.

setups.name: AVWAP Deviation Band (MNQ)
setups.entry: Only fade a clean 2 to 3 sigma stretch with exhaustion, not a band tag inside the trend
setups.bias: The flush stretched the lower bands intraday then reverted to the mean, but fading a one way trend day is dangerous and this only armed on the sharpest stretches.
